Climate_community

Volker Rudolf

2025-05-16

Goals

We will examine how climate variables are linked to different aspects of community state transitions. THis is focused on frog calling data from 8 different ponds across 22 years. Climate data is taking from local weather stations, and frog calling data was converted to transition matrix indicating how community states (i.e. a specific combination of species) transition over time within a year.

Load packages & data

Let’s load the community matrix and climate data (see “Community transition code.Rdm” and “Climate data preparation.Rdm”)

before we get into analysis lets look at correlation between network metrics 

## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

let’s see how those metrics fall out in a multidimensional space in a PCA to better understand they relationship

So two PCA are enough to explain a lot of variation in all these variables, and the first explains by far the most. It’s also interesting that the correlation between variables are robust and don’t change if we ignore small 1, 2, or 3 day gaps. Based on these relationship, we definitely want to keep No_Spec as covariate when we analyze the other metrics, and there is no point in including both totalEdges and Unique nodes since both are so correlated, and total Edges seems to be more different from No species than unique nodes and bit more informative on other aspects of the network.

#Network structure & climate analysis Ok so let’s analyze the network metrics and how they are linked to climate variables. We have to options: (1) use PC1 and PC2 in the analysis which strongly reduces the number of analyses we need. But it also is hard to interpret, and can miss more nuanced relationship of individual variables. So we will do both, PC based GLMM and individual network metric GLMM analyses
